value.first: I'd use the Ferber method (graduated check-ins), with her in her own crib in her own room from night 1, no finishing nights in your bed. It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and a five-year follow-up found no harm to kids. Pick a clear week, set bedtime between 6:30 and 8, do the same 20-30 minute bath, book, bed routine, put her down drowsy but awake, say goodnight and leave. If she's in a toddler bed, the chair method fits better.
value.second: Nights 1-3: when she cries, wait 3 minutes, then 5, then 10, and 10 for every check after that. Checks are 1-2 minutes: lights off, calm voice, same short phrase, no pickup, then leave even mid-cry. Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15. Treat 2am wakings the same way, restarting that night's waits. Expect 30-60+ minutes of protest, and night 2 or 3 may be worse. That's the old habit breaking, not the method failing.
value.third: Nights 4-7, keep stretching: Night 4 12/15/17, Night 5 15/17/20, Night 6 17/20/25, Night 7 20/25/30. It's working when she falls asleep faster each night; many kids are settling in minutes by the end of the week. Never lock or hold her door shut. If she snores, gasps or has pauses in breathing while asleep, that's worth a doctor's look. I'll check in Thursday.
